entities.name: field or element of a structured type

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS a language that supports the specification of expressions.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows the specification of expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: An expression MAY be a template reference, a value reference or a literal without any operation involved.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 expressions may be template references, value references or literals (i.e. no operation is involved), and may be composed of the operators defined in clause 7.1.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: An expression MAY be composed of the predefined operators defined in clause 7.1.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 expressions may be template references, value references or literals (i.e. no operation is involved), and may be composed of the operators defined in clause 7.1.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template CAN be used at the right hand side of an assignment, in parameter passing and in (predefined) functions where template passing is explicitly allowed.
requirements.original: NOTE: Templates can be used at the RHS of assignment, parameter passing and (predefined) functions where template passing is explicitly allowed.

ambiguity.issue: 'RHS' is an abbreviation of the glossary term 'right hand side (of assignment)'.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: An expression IS either a SingleExpression, or a compound expression in assignment notation "{" { FieldReference ":=" ( Expression | "-" ) [","] } "}", or a compound expression in list notation "{" [ { ( Expression | "-" ) [","] } ] "}".
requirements.original:
SingleExpression | 
  "{" { ( FieldReference ":=" ( Expression | "-" )) [","] } "}" | // compound expression
  "{" [ { ( Expression | "-" ) [","] } ] "}" // compound expression

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: An expression MAY be built from other (simple) expressions.
requirements.original: Expressions may be built from other (simple) expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function is invoked in an expression
requirements.canonical: A function used in an expression SHALL have a return clause.
requirements.original: Functions used in expressions shall have a return clause.

requirements.subject: ent:operand
requirements.canonical: An operand of an operator used in an expression SHALL be a value.
requirements.original: The operands of the operators used in an expression shall be values and their root types shall be the types specified for the appropriate operator in the subsequent clauses.

ambiguity.issue: The general rule conflicts with operators such as `isvalue`, `ispresent`, `ischosen` and `isbound`, which accept template instances as operands; reading 1 (rule applies except where an operator clause states otherwise) is chosen.
readings: An operand of an operator used in an expression SHALL be a value, unless the clause of the specific operator explicitly allows templates.
An operand of any operator used in an expression SHALL be a value, without exception.

requirements.subject: ent:operand
requirements.canonical: The root type of an operand of an operator used in an expression SHALL be one of the types specified for that operator in clauses 7.1.1 to 7.1.8.
requirements.original: The operands of the operators used in an expression shall be values and their root types shall be the types specified for the appropriate operator in the subsequent clauses.

requirements.subject: ent:operand
requirements.canonical: When an expression is evaluated, the evaluated value of an operand SHALL be completely initialized, unless the clause of the specific operator explicitly states otherwise.
requirements.original: a) At the point, when an expression is evaluated, the evaluated values of the operands used in expressions shall be completely initialized except where explicitly stated otherwise in the specific clause of the operator.

requirements.subject: ent:operand
requirements.canonical: The root type of an operand SHALL be one of the types specified for the operator applied to it.
requirements.original: b) The root types of the operands shall be the types specified for the appropriate operand.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence says 'types specified for the appropriate operand', where 'appropriate operator' is meant (compare 7.0-s007); it restates 7.0-007b.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` SHALL NOT be used as an operand of an expression other than the equal (`==`) and not equal (`!=`) operators.
requirements.original: c) With the exception of the equality and non-equality operators, the special value null shall not be used as an operand of expressions (see clause 7.1.3).

requirements.subject: ent:field
requirements.condition: the field or element is referenced in the expression
requirements.canonical: A field or element of a structured type that is referenced in an expression SHALL contain a completely initialized value.
requirements.original: This means also that all fields and elements of structured types referenced in an expression shall contain completely initialized values, while other fields and elements, not used in the expression, may be uninitialized or contain omit.

requirements.subject: ent:field
requirements.condition: the field or element is not used in the expression
requirements.canonical: A field or element of a structured type that is not used in an expression MAY be uninitialized or contain `omit`.
requirements.original: This means also that all fields and elements of structured types referenced in an expression shall contain completely initialized values, while other fields and elements, not used in the expression, may be uninitialized or contain omit.

requirements.subject: ent:compound-expression
requirements.canonical: An expression of a record, set, record of, set of, array, union or anytype type IS written in assignment notation or value list notation.
requirements.original: Assignment or list notations are used for expressions of record, set, record of, set of, array, union and anytype types.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether both notations apply to every listed type; list notation is not allowed for union and anytype, and assignment notation is not used for record of/set of/array (which use index notation). Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: An expression of a record, set, record of, set of, array, union or anytype type IS written in the notation (assignment or value list) that is allowed for that type.
An expression of any of the types record, set, record of, set of, array, union and anytype MAY be written in either assignment notation or value list notation.

requirements.subject: ent:predefined-operator
requirements.canonical: A predefined operator MAY be used in the terms of a TTCN-3 expression.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports a number of predefined operators that may be used in the terms of TTCN-3 expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:predefined-operator
requirements.canonical: A predefined operator IS a member of one of the categories arithmetic, list, relational, logical, bitwise, shift, rotate or presence checking operators.
requirements.original: The predefined operators fall into seven categories:

ambiguity.issue: The sentence states 'seven categories' but the following list a) to h) has eight entries; table 5 also names the list operator category 'String operators'. The list of eight is chosen.
readings: The predefined operators fall into the eight categories listed in items a) to h).
The predefined operators fall into seven categories, one of the listed items being redundant.

requirements.subject: ent:arithmetic-operator
requirements.canonical: The arithmetic operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
requirements.original: a) arithmetic operators;

requirements.subject: ent:list-operator
requirements.canonical: The list operator category IS a category of predefined operators.
requirements.original: b) list operator;

requirements.subject: ent:relational-operator
requirements.canonical: The relational operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
requirements.original: c) relational operators;

requirements.subject: ent:logical-operator
requirements.canonical: The logical operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
requirements.original: d) logical operators;

requirements.subject: ent:bitwise-operator
requirements.canonical: The bitwise operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
requirements.original: e) bitwise operators;

requirements.subject: ent:shift-operator
requirements.canonical: The shift operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
requirements.original: f) shift operators;

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-operator
requirements.canonical: The rotate operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
requirements.original: g) rotate operators;

requirements.subject: ent:presence-checking-operator
requirements.canonical: The presence checking operators category IS a category of predefined operators.
requirements.original: h) presence checking operators.

requirements.subject: ent:operand
requirements.canonical: When an expression is evaluated, the evaluated value used as an operand of an operator SHALL be completely initialized, unless the operand is explicitly allowed to be partially initialized.
requirements.original: a) When an expression is evaluated, the evaluated values used as the operands of operators shall be completely initialized, except for those operands for which it is explicitly allowed to be partially initialized (see clause 11.1).

requirements.subject: ent:operator-precedence
requirements.canonical: An operator listed in a row of table 6 IS of equal precedence to every other operator listed in the same row.
requirements.original: Within any row in this table, the listed operators have equal precedence.

requirements.subject: ent:operator-precedence
requirements.condition: more than one operator of equal precedence appears in an expression
requirements.canonical: If more than one operator of equal precedence appears in an expression, each operation IS evaluated in left-to-right order.
requirements.original: If more than one operator of equal precedence appears in an expression, the operations are evaluated from left to right.

requirements.subject: ent:parenthesized-expression
requirements.canonical: Parentheses MAY be used to group operands in an expression.
requirements.original: Parentheses may be used to group operands in expressions, in which case a parenthesized expression has the highest precedence for evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:parenthesized-expression
requirements.canonical: A parenthesized expression IS of the highest precedence for evaluation.
requirements.original: Parentheses may be used to group operands in expressions, in which case a parenthesized expression has the highest precedence for evaluation.
